Package neqsim.mcp.runners

Class McpRequestContext

java.lang.Object
neqsim.mcp.runners.McpRequestContext
public final class McpRequestContext extends Object
Per-request caller identity for the NeqSim MCP server.

The MCP tool facade does not accept credentials as tool arguments — secrets must never travel through model-visible tool parameters. Instead the transport layer (stdio launcher, HTTP filter, or OAuth resource-server filter) resolves the caller once and binds a McpRequestContext.Principal to the serving thread. Governance code such as IndustrialProfile.enforceAccess(String) and SecurityRunner.checkAccess(String, String) then reads the bound principal instead of receiving a hard-coded null credential.

When nothing is bound, current() returns McpRequestContext.Principal.anonymous(). That keeps local desktop usage (security disabled) working unchanged while allowing enforcement to fail closed when security is enabled.

Typical transport usage: 

 McpRequestContext.set(Principal.ofApiKey(apiKeyFromHeader));
 try {
   return tool.invoke(arguments);
 } finally {
   McpRequestContext.clear();
 }
